content: 1. Increase the dose of enzalutamide from 160 mg daily to 240 mg daily if a strong CYP3A4 inducer is co-administered. If the strong CYP3A4 inducer is discontinued, revert the enzalutamide dose to the pre-induction level. Close monitoring is required. 2. Rifampin reduces the levels or efficacy of eplerenone by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. In serious cases, consider alternative therapies. 3. Rifampin decreases the levels or efficacy of erdafitinib by altering its metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Erdafitinib increases rifampin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, separate administration by at least 6 hours before or after P-gp substrate administration with a narrow therapeutic index. 4. Rifampin reduces the levels or efficacy of ergotamine by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is required. 5. Rifampin decreases the levels or efficacy of erlotinib by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is required. 6. Rifampin reduces the levels or efficacy of erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate forms) by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is required. 7. Rifampin decreases the levels or efficacy of escitalopram by inducing hepatic CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Rifampin reduces the levels or efficacy of esomeprazole by inducing hepatic CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Rifampin decreases the levels or efficacy of estradiol (oral and vaginal forms) by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is required. 10. Rifampin reduces the levels or efficacy of conjugated synthetic estrogens and esterified estrogens by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is required. 11. Rifampin decreases the levels or efficacy of estropipate by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is required. 12. Rifampin reduces the levels or efficacy of eszopiclone by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Zopiclone AUC is reduced by 80% with rifampin co-administration, and a similar effect is expected with eszopiclone. 13. Ethanol decreases rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents and is more likely with chronic ethanol use. The clinical significance is unknown. 14. Rifampin reduces the levels or efficacy of ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 15. Rifampin decreases the levels or efficacy of ethosuximide by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 16. Rifampin reduces the levels or efficacy of ethotoin by inducing hepatic CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Rifampin decreases the levels or efficacy of etonogestrel by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Rifampin reduces the levels or efficacy of etoposide by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Rifampin decreases the levels or efficacy of etrasimod by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Rifampin is a strong CYP3A4 inducer and moderately induces CYP2C8 and CYP2C9, reducing systemic exposure to etrasimod. 20. Rifampin reduces the levels or efficacy of etravirine by inducing hepatic CYP2C19, CYP2C9/10, and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is required. 21. Rifampin decreases the levels or efficacy of eucalyptus by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Rifampin reduces the levels or efficacy of everolimus by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration is contraindicated. 23. Rifampin decreases the levels or efficacy of exemestane by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. For patients on potent CYP3A4 inducers, the recommended exemestane dose is 50 mg daily after a meal. 24. Rifampin reduces the levels or efficacy of fedratinib by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. The effect of co-administering a strong CYP3A4 inducer with fedratinib has not been studied. 25. Rifampin decreases the levels or efficacy of felbamate by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Rifampin reduces the levels or efficacy of felodipine by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Rifampin decreases the levels or efficacy of fenfluramine by an unspecified mechanism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Co-administration with serotonin-increasing drugs may increase the risk of serotonin syndrome. 28. Rifampin reduces the levels or efficacy of fentanyl (intranasal, transdermal, transmucosal) by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inducers may lead to reduced fentanyl plasma concentrations, lack of efficacy, or withdrawal syndrome in dependent patients. After stopping a CYP3A4 inducer, fentanyl plasma concentrations may increase, potentially prolonging therapeutic and adverse effects. 29. Rifampin decreases the levels or efficacy of fesoterodine by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Rifampin increases the levels or efficacy of fexinidazole by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Fexinidazole decreases rifampin levels by inducing hepatic CYP2B6 metabolism, which may reduce plasma concentrations of CYP2B6 substrates. 31. Rifampin reduces the levels or efficacy of fexofenadine by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance is unknown. 32. Rifampin decreases the levels or efficacy of finasteride by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Rifampin reduces the levels or efficacy of finerenone by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Rifampin decreases the levels or efficacy of flibanserin by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Strong CYP3A4 inducers significantly reduce flibanserin systemic exposure. 35. Rifampin reduces fluconazole levels by increasing metabolism. Fluconazole decreases rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 36. Rifampin decreases the levels or efficacy of fludrocortisone by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is required. 37. Rifampin reduces the levels or efficacy of flurazepam by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Rifampin decreases the levels or efficacy of flurbiprofen by inducing hepatic CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 39. Rifampin increases fluvastatin toxicity by an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rifampin reduces fluvastatin levels by inducing hepatic CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 40. Rifampin decreases the levels or efficacy of fosamprenavir by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 41. Rifampin reduces the levels or efficacy of fosaprepitant by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Rifampin decreases fosinopril levels by increasing metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 43. Rifampin reduces the levels or efficacy of fosphenytoin by inducing hepatic CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Fostamatinib increases rifampin levels by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Rifampin reduces fostamatinib levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 45. Rifampin decreases the levels or efficacy of fostemsavir by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Fostemsavir (a prodrug) co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers significantly reduces temsavir (active moiety) plasma concentrations, potentially leading to loss of virologic response and resistance. 46. Rifampin reduces the levels or efficacy of frovatriptan by inducing hepatic CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 47. Rifampin decreases the levels or efficacy of fruquintinib by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Rifampin reduces the levels or efficacy of futibatinib by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with dual P-gp and strong CYP3A inducers may reduce futibatinib efficacy.
